newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine tax revenue hits Convertibility record.
newsitem.headline: Argentine tax revenue hits Convertibility record.

text.p: Argentina's tax revenue in May reached $4.6 billion, an increase of 28.6 percent on May last year and of 17.3 percent versus April this year, the government said Tuesday.
"It's the highest level of revenue since Convertibility began," the Undersecretary of Tax Revenue Policy, Guillermo Rodriguez Use, told reporters.

The official said the sharp rise in total revenue, which strips out contributions to the private pension-fund system, was mainly due to privatized oil giant YPF SA YPF.BA paying income tax this year for the first time since its sell-off.
He said that boost the income tax total, which was $1.29 billion, by more than $200 million.

Rodriguez Use said there was also a boost from the change in the personal income tax deadline this year to May, instead of June as it was last year. Revenue was swollen by more economic activity and less tax evasion, said the official.

Value-added tax collected by the customs office rose 31.1 percent May on May due to higher imports, while the 12 percent April-May rise in VAT collected by the DGI tax office was due to higher domestic economic activity, he said.
Personal wealth tax rose by 1,300 percent year on year to $68.8 million.
The official forecast that June's overall tax collection would be between $3.9-4.0 billion, compared to June 1996's $3.6 billion.
